To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
active EMI filters can be used to reduce the volume of passive EMI filters in power electronic converters.
AEFs can be implemented in different power converters and can be designed for both differential mode and common mode noises.
AEFs are a viable option to reduce the volume of passive components in power converters and that the design and implementation of AEFs depend on the type of converter, noise and topology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a high efficiency active EMI filter for power electronic converters.
the design of a new active filter for the mitigation of EMI noise in power converters.
the design, modeling and control of power electronic converters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
active EMI filters are a viable solution for reducing passive component count in power converters, especially in the case of high switching frequency and high power applications.
AEFs are an effective method for conducted noise reduction and can be implemented in a wide variety of power converters.
the AEFs have been proven to be a viable solution to mitigate the conducted EMI noise in power electronic converters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AEFs can reduce the size and cost of the passive components, but the AEFs have a higher cost and power loss.
the AEFs can be a viable solution to the passive EMI filter bottleneck.
the active filters can be used to reduce the size and weight of the EMI filters in power converters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AEFs are not a panacea and should be considered only if there are no other options.
the AEFs can provide significant reduction in passive components and hence increase the power density of the power converters.

the design of an active EMI filter depends upon the converter and type of noise (differential mode or common mode) to be attenuated and the AEF design is a complex process that needs to take into consideration several aspects such as noise sensing, noise cancellation, auxiliary power supply, and protection.
